subject: Notice: StreamingGate analytics processor deprecation — evidence & routing ask
messages:
From: StreamingGate Inc. <security@streaminggate.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@streaminggate.com
Date: 2028-08-22T09:12:00Z
Subject: Planned deprecation of ‘SG-Analytics’ processor (action requested)

Hi Kimberly,

I’m reaching out to notify you that StreamingGate will retire the ‘SG-Analytics’ processing pipeline on 2028-09-30. This affects the telemetry enrichment step we currently perform for Redwood customers in our EU cluster.

What we’re changing:
- SG-Analytics (v1) will be decommissioned and replaced by SG-Analytics-v2 (new vendor flow) on 2028-09-30.
- The replacement route will add a third-party aggregation step in our US processing region unless customers explicitly opt into onshore routing.

What we are sending you now:
- deprecation_notice.pdf (summary and timeline)
- new_processor_manifest.csv (list of subprocessors and their roles)

Requested action by 2028-08-29:
1) Confirm whether GoodWave accepts processing through the new SG-Analytics-v2 route (which may transiently egress to the US).
2) If not acceptable, provide requirements for onshore/EU-only routing or escrow arrangements so we can propose a remediation plan.
3) Share any evidence you need (SOC 2, flow diagrams, DPIA excerpts) and we’ll attach them to a follow-up.

We realize this is short notice for some customers. If helpful, we can provide a temporary dual-run configuration to avoid disruption while we finalize routing.

Best,
Emma Lawson
Head of Security Programs, StreamingGate
[Attachment: deprecation_notice.pdf (PDF, 125KB)]
[Attachment: new_processor_manifest.csv (CSV, 8KB)]

From: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
To: Emma.Lawson@streaminggate.com, security@streaminggate.com
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com, rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2028-08-22T12:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Planned deprecation of ‘SG-Analytics’ processor (action requested)

Emma —

Thanks for the heads-up and the manifest. Quick responses below and a few asks from our side before we sign off:

1) We cannot accept any egress of GoodWave telemetry outside the EU without explicit controls. Please confirm whether SG-Analytics-v2 will export raw or pseudonymized logs to the US, and which subprocessors in the CSV have access to raw identifiers.

2) We will need: a) a clear data flow diagram showing processing steps and locations, b) SOC 2 Type II report for any new subprocessor with access to telemetry, and c) a transitional plan guaranteeing EU-only routing or escrow if you intend to use a US-based aggregator.

3) Timeline: 2028-09-30 is tight for our legal and procurement review. Please hold the deprecation for GoodWave to 2028-11-15 or provide a temporary onshore routing option.

Cc’d Lauren and Rishi to flag risk and to coordinate procurement/legal asks.

Thanks — we’d like to avoid rework for the GoodWave integration.

—Kimberly Park
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1-415-555-0192

From: rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
To: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com, lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2028-08-23T08:40:00Z
Subject: RE: Planned deprecation of ‘SG-Analytics’ processor (action requested)

Kimberly / Lauren —

Quick note on risk and proposed ask to StreamingGate:

- If SG-Analytics-v2 performs aggregation in the US and holds raw telemetry for >24 hours, this is not acceptable for GoodWave’s EU residency requirement. We should ask for either EU-only processing endpoints or per-customer tokenization that prevents identifiable exports.

- Suggested immediate actions for procurement/legal to send: a) request a SOC 2 Type II for SG-Analytics-v2 and any subcontractors; b) require an explicit statement of which subprocessors will have access to unredacted telemetry and the jurisdictions they operate in; c) insist on a temporary onshore (EU) routing for GoodWave during the migration window.

I drafted a short risk summary you can send to their security and procurement teams. Attaching — please edit as you see fit.

-Rishi
Senior Manager, Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: risk_summary.docx (DOCX, 42KB)]

From: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
To: Emma.Lawson@streaminggate.com, security@streaminggate.com
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com, rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2028-08-25T15:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Planned deprecation of ‘SG-Analytics’ processor (action requested)

Emma —

Following internal review we require the following to approve the change for GoodWave:

1) Confirmation in writing that no raw telemetry (including IP, device IDs, or user identifiers) will be egressed to the US for GoodWave data; if the new pipeline cannot guarantee this, provide an EU-only routing option.
2) SOC 2 Type II report and scope for SG-Analytics-v2 and any subcontractors with telemetry access.
3) Data flow diagram (high-level) showing where tokenization/aggregation occurs and retention windows for raw vs. aggregated material.
4) A temporary hold on the decommission date for GoodWave to 2028-11-15 OR an immediate EU dual-run to avoid service disruption.

If you can provide the items above by 2028-08-29 we will circulate internally and aim to provide a formal acceptance using the attached template. If you prefer, we can put this into a short MOU — procurement will lead that.

Attaching our acceptance template for your convenience.

Thanks — we appreciate quick collaboration to avoid breaking GoodWave’s SLA.

Best regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: subprocessor_acceptance_template.docx (DOCX, 12KB)]
